title: Check rack and everyday cargo setup
summary: Verify the rack, compatible luggage and load placement before carrying ordinary commuting or shopping cargo.

tools.name: Rack/bicycle load information
tools.note: Use the actual rack, bicycle and luggage manufacturer's limits.

steps.title: Inspect the rack and its mounts
steps.instruction: Look for cracks, bending, looseness, missing hardware or movement at the rack-to-frame mounting points.
steps.why: The rack is a load path into the bicycle frame; damaged or loose mounts can compromise luggage support.
steps.warning: Do not tighten rack hardware to an invented torque. Use the actual rack/frame instructions.
steps.check: The rack and visible mounting points show no obvious damage or unsafe looseness.

steps.title: Confirm the real system limits
steps.instruction: Check the permitted rack load and any lower limits imposed by the bicycle, luggage system or mounting hardware before loading.
steps.why: A rack's capacity is not a universal property of every bicycle that can physically accept it.
steps.warning: Use the lowest applicable load limit in the actual rack/bicycle/luggage system.
steps.check: The intended cargo is within the applicable documented limits.

steps.title: Secure the load away from wheels and controls
steps.instruction: Attach compatible luggage so straps, hooks and loose material cannot enter the rear wheel, brake or drivetrain. Keep the load stable rather than able to swing freely.
steps.why: Loose luggage can shift handling or become entangled with moving parts.
steps.warning: Never allow loose straps or fabric to hang near the wheel, rotor, chain or sprocket.
steps.check: Cargo is secure, stable and clear of moving parts.

steps.title: Do a controlled handling check
steps.instruction: Before normal riding, push and then ride the loaded bicycle at low speed in a safe area. Confirm steering, braking and stand-over/parking behavior remain predictable.
steps.why: Added mass and its position can change steering feel, braking distance and parking stability.
steps.warning: If the bicycle feels unstable or the load shifts, stop and change the setup before entering traffic or normal riding.
steps.check: The loaded bicycle remains predictable during the controlled check.
